claims.text: The dominant rate-controlling mechanism in dynamically loaded solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is activation of partial dislocations.
Co-free FeNiCrMn has sufficiently reduced stacking-fault energy to favor partial-dislocation activity and twinning.
Lower temperatures and higher strain rates increase partial-dislocation activity in FeNiCrMn.
Activated partial dislocations form deformation twins in the FCC FeNiCrMn matrix.
Twin formation enhances strain hardening in FeNiCrMn.
The proposed twinning-mediated strain hardening increases dynamic strength.
The proposed twinning mechanism increases dynamic ductility.
At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, ordinary dislocation slip dominates over twinning.
Recovery and cross-slip dominate deformation at higher temperatures or lower strain rates.
The increased importance of recovery, cross-slip, and ordinary slip diminishes strain-rate sensitivity.
The proposed homogenized and solutionized FeNiCrMn starting material is single-phase FCC with minimal prior deformation.
Yield strength and flow stress of FeNiCrMn increase from quasi-static to high-strain-rate loading.
Yield strength and flow stress increase by approximately 50–100% from quasi-static to high-strain-rate loading.
Twin-boundary density is greater at low temperatures and high strain rates.
Fewer deformation twins form at elevated temperatures or slow strain rates.
Co-free FeNiCrMn has comparable or slightly higher dynamic strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under similar loading conditions.
Co-free FeNiCrMn has comparable or slightly higher dynamic ductility than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under similar loading conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies from cryogenic temperatures to approximately 650 K and from 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.
Outside the stated temperature and strain-rate range, diffusion or phase transformations may alter the deformation mechanism.
Dynamic strength should scale with the measured twin fraction.

contradictions.description: The intervention and falsification experiment include testing at 673 K, whereas the stated applicability boundary ends at approximately 650 K and says processes outside that range may alter the mechanism.
